corrections_to_earlier_packets: #219 confirmed: the (+0x20, +0x8) setb/sbb signum idiom and the +0x28 pair / +0x30 link / +0x38 word are the same ones the slot-insert helper uses; this helper re-splices chains with that idiom after unlinking.
#222 confirmed: this helper is the slot-remove callee its next question pointed at; its three callers are 0x636359f, 0x6363a6f and 0x63b0847.

head_path.right_child_present: [slot+8] := 0, then merge walk over the successor chain (0x63acd84)
head_path.slot_second_word: written only as 0 on this path; its semantic identity is unresolved

merge_walks.note: The (+0x20, +0x8) signum idiom compares adjacent chain nodes while re-splicing, not the target node: the target arrives as an argument and is never searched for by key.

nonhead_fast_paths.guard: [node+0x28] = P nonzero and [P+0x38] == node, else the merge walks run

unresolved: The global invariant of the slot chain (sorted list versus tree, and the key order direction) is not settled by these bytes: the rotation block at 0x63ad078 assigns the head's +0x38 side by key comparison in a way no plain BST reading explains.
The semantic identity of the slot's second word ([slot+8]): zeroed on insert-before (#219) and on head removal with a +0x38 side, incremented on after-head insert (#219).

Which of the three callers is #222's collect sibling is not mapped here; the two 0x6363-region callers are structural twins and the 0x63b0-region caller pairs the remove with a second call to 0x63abcf0 on the same slot.
The purpose of the paired callee 0x63abcf0 and of the 0x63b0780..0x63b097f caller FDE as a whole.
